holidays.name: National Croissant Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the buttery, flaky, crescent-shaped pastry by eating as many as your heart (and cholesterol levels) can handle. Plain, chocolate-filled, or stuffed with ham and cheese, every layer counts.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday, popularized by food-day calendars. The croissant itself descends from the Austrian kipferl, and was popularized in France in the 1830s after Austrian August Zang opened a Viennese bakery in Paris.
holidays.funFact: A proper croissant can have around 27 layers of dough and butter, created by a lamination process of repeated folding and rolling.

holidays.name: Day of the Escaped Cow? No, Actually: Time Management Day
holidays.description: Better known as National Time Management Day, it is a day to take stock of your calendar, ditch the procrastination, and finally stop pressing snooze. Ironically, many people put off celebrating it until later.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance in the productivity and self-help community, held to encourage people to start the year with more disciplined scheduling habits.
holidays.funFact: The idea of scheduling your day into blocks dates back to Benjamin Franklin, who famously planned his days with a daily schedule asking 'What good shall I do this day?'

holidays.name: National Inane Answering Message Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to recording ridiculous, silly, or downright nonsensical voicemail greetings. Think singing, fake accents, or pretending you have been abducted by aliens.
holidays.origin: Created by Kevin Zraly? No, by quirky-holiday creator Gary Lee Dwight? Uncertain. It is a tongue-in-cheek unofficial observance that grew with the rise of answering machines in the 1980s and 1990s.
holidays.funFact: Early answering machine greetings became a pop culture staple, and a funny outgoing message was famously used as a gag in the sitcom Seinfeld, where George recorded a 'Believe it or not, George isn't at home' message.

holidays.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Observance? No: Backward Day
holidays.description: Backward Day invites people to wear their clothes backward, eat dessert before dinner, and say goodbye instead of hello. It is a day for flipping norms on their heads, literally.
holidays.origin: An unofficial and playful observance traditionally celebrated on January 30 in some calendars, tied to whimsical children's celebrations and classroom activities, with no single documented founder.
holidays.funFact: Many schools use Backward Day as a classroom activity, where kids wear their clothes inside out and even hold class schedules in reverse order.

holidays.name: Univers of Cheese: National Bubble Wrap Appreciation Day
holidays.description: Celebrated on the last Monday of January, this day honors the sweet, sweet sound of popping plastic bubbles. Stress relief has never been so crackly, and it is perfectly acceptable to pop at your desk.
holidays.origin: Started by radio station WFMU? Actually, it was launched by Indiana University's radio station WFHB in Bloomington, Indiana, in 2001, in honor of the packing material's strangely satisfying nature.
holidays.funFact: Bubble Wrap was originally invented in 1957 as textured wallpaper, not packing material, and failed spectacularly in that market.
